evidence.requirements: Every functional requirement is implemented with the exact labels the brief asks for. The start page lists title, date and time, price and "<n> seats left" (TastingCard.tsx:26-39, start.jpg). Each tasting has a "Book <title>" link (TastingCard.tsx:50). The form has Name, Email and Guests (1-8) fields and a Book button (BookingPage.tsx:102-133). Errors appear next to the field they concern (form.jpg). The confirmation shows the heading "Booking confirmed", the tasting, the guests, the total and the reference (ConfirmationPage.tsx:32-51, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and a Sign in button, and the password comes from STAFF_PASSWORD (index.ts:23, StaffPage.tsx:67-79). Staff see bookings grouped by tasting with a Cancel button, and cancelling frees the seats (staff.jpg, bookingStore.ts:105). The stack is React, React Router, React Hook Form, Zod, Tailwind and Express, as the brief suggests. Two parts are only partly met. (1) 'Polished look': the brand name in the header is nearly invisible on every page (start.jpg). (2) 'Usable on a phone': the README admits this was never checked in a browser (README.md:86), and there is no phone screenshot. Bookings are kept in a JSON file, which the brief allows.
evidence.correctness: The seat check and the insert run synchronously in one call (bookingStore.ts:89-103), so concurrent requests cannot overbook in a single Node process. The server rejects guests above the seats left with a 409 error attached to the guests field (tastings.ts:92-95). The client resolver reads the latest seat count and refetches after a conflict (BookingPage.tsx:47-54, 175). Validation is shared between client and server: name and email are trimmed and length-limited, and guests must be a whole number from 1 to 8 (bookingSchema.ts:14-34). Cancelling removes the booking and frees its seats (bookingStore.ts:105-110), and a 404 from a cancel refreshes the staff list (StaffPage.tsx:107). Malformed JSON, oversized bodies and unknown tastings are handled (errors.ts:30-36). A corrupt data file stops startup instead of silently losing bookings (bookingStore.ts:131-145). Minor gaps: bookings are still accepted after a tasting has started; the staff 'seats left' text is always green, even at 0 (StaffPage.tsx:172); and a retry after a lost response books twice (README.md:81).
evidence.security: React escapes all output, and there is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. The password check hashes both values with SHA-256 and compares them with timingSafeEqual (staffAuth.ts:34-36). Session tokens are 32 random bytes (staffAuth.ts:40), sent in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, marked Secure in production, and expire after 8 hours (staff.ts:28,47). Sign-out removes the session on the server (staff.ts:51-56). Staff routes are protected by a guard (staff.ts:81-89). Failed logins, bookings and reference lookups are rate-limited (app.ts:37-39). Helmet is enabled, JSON bodies are limited to 10kb, and the booking endpoint requires a JSON content type (tastings.ts:78-82). The public confirmation endpoint never returns names or emails (api.test.ts:174-184). There are no secrets in the code, and the server refuses to start without a password (staffAuth.ts:6-12). TRUST_PROXY=true is rejected on purpose to prevent X-Forwarded-For spoofing (index.ts:52-58).
evidence.code_quality: The structure is clear: client/server/shared, with one Zod schema used on both sides and a small store class. Names are good, and errors go through a single ApiError envelope (errors.ts). Functions are small, and the comments explain why rather than what. Minor issues: the resolver needs an `as unknown as` double cast (BookingPage.tsx:50), long Tailwind button class strings are copied across components instead of using a Button component (BookingPage.tsx:130, StaffPage.tsx:77, TastingCard.tsx:48), and the import order in ConfirmationPage.tsx:6 is untidy.
evidence.tests: About 60 tests in Vitest cover the main behaviour. The store tests cover exact-fit bookings, overbooking, cancelling, persistence, file mode and corrupt files (bookingStore.test.ts). Supertest API tests cover validation errors per field, the 409 seats conflict, 'fully booked', auth, cookie flags, rate limits, cancelling and a 500 error that hides details (api.test.ts). Component tests check the exact labels and button names from the brief, accessible error descriptions, the confirmation flow, a fully booked tasting, staff cancel with confirm and decline, and session expiry (BookingPage/StaffPage/TastingsPage tests). Gaps: no test for concurrent bookings even though the spec has that scenario (guest-tasting-booking/spec.md:85-88); the client tests run against a mocked fetch, so there is no end-to-end or browser test; and none of the tests would catch the header contrast bug.
evidence.ux_design: The burgundy, gold and cream palette with serif headings feels right for a winery (start.jpg). The cards are clear and the Book buttons stand out. The form shows a red field border with an inline message (form.jpg) and a live total in the 'Your visit' sidebar. The confirmation card is clean and puts the reference in a monospace font (confirmation.jpg). The staff view groups bookings in tidy tables with 'No bookings yet' when a tasting is empty (staff.jpg). The fully booked state has a badge and hides the booking link (TastingCard.tsx:19-23,43-44). Flaws: the brand name 'Weingut Kieselbrunnen' is dark burgundy on a dark burgundy header and almost unreadable on every page (all screenshots). The global `a { text-wine-700 }` rule (styles.css:44-46) overrides the header's text-cream-50 because the brand Link (Layout.tsx:8-9) has no text colour of its own. The Sign out button sits slightly out of line (staff.jpg), and the phone layout was never verified (README.md:86).
evidence.accessibility: Labels are linked to their inputs with htmlFor/useId. Invalid fields get aria-invalid and aria-describedby pointing at the error text (TextField.tsx:17-31). Error notices use role=alert and status notices use role=status (Notice.tsx:15). There is a landmark nav plus header, main and footer (Layout.tsx). Sections are labelled by their headings, tables use th scope=col, the actions column has an sr-only header (StaffPage.tsx:181-185), and the date uses a time element (TastingCard.tsx:29). A visible focus outline is set globally (styles.css:48-51), and the page declares lang=en. React Hook Form moves focus to the first invalid field by default. The main failure: the header brand link fails WCAG contrast badly (wine-700 #6b1e2e on wine-900 #3d0c18, about 1.5:1; start.jpg). In addition, inline field errors are not live regions; they are only announced through aria-describedby once the field has focus.
evidence.simplicity: The dependencies are mainstream and match the brief (Express, React Router, RHF, Zod, Tailwind, Helmet, express-rate-limit). The total amount of code is modest. One custom useLoad hook (useLoad.ts) replaces a data-fetching library, which is reasonable at this size. A few extras go slightly beyond the brief, such as the reference-lookup limiter and the parsing of the trust-proxy hop count, but they are small and well justified.
evidence.maintainability: The README covers install, build and run, an environment variable table, development mode, the test, coverage and typecheck commands, the code layout, behaviour notes and an honest list of known gaps. OpenSpec specs describe both capabilities with scenarios (openspec/specs/*). package-lock.json is present and engines requires node>=22. Weaknesses: there is no CI configuration (no workflow files), no changelog or release process, no .nvmrc or pinned Node version, and no ADRs. The README contradicts the code: it says to set `TRUST_PROXY` to `true` (README.md:31), but index.ts:54-55 exits on startup when the value is 'true'. The README also points to `openspec/changes/tasting-bookings/` (README.md:74), which is not in the repository. Staff have no guide beyond two README lines.

unmet_requirements: Polished look and feel only partly met: the winery name in the header is nearly invisible on every page (dark burgundy text on a dark burgundy header; styles.css:44-46 overrides the colour set in Layout.tsx:6-9).
'Usable on a phone' is not verified: README.md:86 admits the phone layout was never checked in a browser, and there is no phone screenshot.
strengths: Solid booking core: the seat check and insert run synchronously so seats cannot be oversold, one Zod schema validates on both client and server, and seat conflicts show as an error on the Guests field and refresh the seat count.

Strong staff security: SHA-256 digests compared in constant time, random session tokens in an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie with server-side expiry and sign-out, rate limits, Helmet, a body size limit, and no personal data on the public confirmation endpoint.

Meaningful test suite (store, API through supertest, components) that checks the brief's exact labels, the error messages next to fields, overbooking, cancelling and auth behaviour, backed by OpenSpec scenarios and a thorough README.
issues: The brand name 'Weingut Kieselbrunnen' in the header is almost invisible on every page (about 1.5:1 contrast) because the global `a` colour rule overrides the header text colour. It is both a visual flaw and a WCAG failure (start.jpg, styles.css:44-46, Layout.tsx:8-9).

There is no CI pipeline, release or versioning process, or pinned Node version. The README contradicts the code: TRUST_PROXY=true is documented, but the server exits on that value (README.md:31 vs index.ts:54). It also links a missing openspec/changes path (README.md:74).

The phone layout was never verified, there is no test for the concurrent booking scenario in the spec, and there are smaller gaps: bookings are accepted after a tasting has started, a retry after a lost response books twice, and the staff 'seats left' text stays green at 0.
review.verdict: This is a well-engineered, secure and well-tested booking app that meets every functional requirement in the brief and looks fitting for a winery. Before shipping I would fix the nearly invisible winery name in the header, correct the README errors, and add CI and a phone check. None of these is hard to fix.
